messages:
nora: Following the postmortem, we need a short checklist of owners and delivery dates for the KV-cache memory/fragmentation work. I want one message per owner with a target and rollback plan.

sam: I'll take the heap-sample collector and nightly trace retention. Plan: wire collector + ship to s3. ETA: 2 weeks for infra + 2 more for dashboards. Rollback: collector is read-only so low risk.

oliver: I'll drive compaction behavior changes. Proposal: threshold-driven compaction (fragmentation > 0.55 triggers quick-pass) + weekend full compaction. Risk: CPU spike during compaction; rollback: revert compaction schedule. ETA: prototype in 1 week, canary in next deployment window.

leila: allocator improvements: I'll prepare a small allocator shim to reduce cross-shard free-list volatility. Design doc by EOD, bench + safe flag for rollout. ETA: design + bench 3 weeks, staged rollout 6 weeks.

maya: I'll own deployment/runbook and the emergency OOM playbook. Runbook will include automatic fallback toggles and manual kill/scale steps. ETA: runbook draft 3 days.

chris: I'll add tenant-scoped telemetry and noisy-tenant alerts. Suggest two signals: sustained allocation rate per-tenant > 2x baseline for 10m, and per-tenant fragmentation ratio > 0.4. I can land alert rules this week.

engbot: deploy-bot: canary environment (kv-frag-rc1) spun up with current gc-branch.

nora: circuit-breaker + adaptive eviction: I'll build a light path that starts evicting lower-priority keys when heap > 75% of limit and enables per-route throttling. Fallback: emergency denylist + route-shepherding to keep critical traffic. ETA: initial PR in 4 working days.

sam: quick note: sampling rate at 1% missed spikes. We'll run 5% for 48 hours during the next low-traffic window to get better signal.

oliver: reproduction checklist I'm owning: workload profiles to hit fragmentation fast: 1) mix of 64B writes + large deletes, 2) sustained lease holders, 3) tenant churn. Will publish loadgen configs.

leila: implementation strategy: landing a shim first to toggle at runtime, then swap allocator. That gives instant rollback via flag.

chris: alerting + oncall: please add pager mapping to eng-runtime oncall for the two new alerts. I recommend critical severity for OOM risk.

engbot: alert created: KV_TENANT_NOISY and KV_FRAGMENT_THRESHOLD. Pager: eng-runtime oncall.

sam: consolidated AI list (we'll use the postmortem issue to track):
- AI-101: heap-sample collector + dashboards -> owner: sam -> ETA: 2w infra + 2w dashboards -> status: in-progress
- AI-102: threshold-driven compaction + weekend full-pass -> owner: oliver -> ETA: prototype 1w, canary next window -> status: prototyping
- AI-103: allocator shim + bench -> owner: leila -> ETA: design EOD, impl 6w -> status: todo
- AI-104: runtime circuit-breaker + adaptive eviction -> owner: nora -> ETA: PR in 4 working days -> status: in-progress
- AI-105: tenant telemetry + noisy-tenant alerts -> owner: chris -> ETA: alert rules this week -> status: todo
- AI-106: rollout/runbook + emergency OOM playbook -> owner: maya -> ETA: runbook draft 3d -> status: todo

maya: please react with a quick "ok" or an alternate ETA. We'll have a weekly check-in on Fri to ensure no drift.

oliver: ok for dates. I'll have loadgen configs by Wed.

sam: ok on ETA. Will start 5% sampling tonight in staging and share sample sinks.

nora: ok. I'll post a short design for the adaptive eviction heuristic tomorrow.

leila: design doc up in /docs; will link PR when ready. 6w still accurate.

chris: alert rules done; pushing to prod after review.

nora: one more ask 12: can we add a metric for longest-lived free-list holes? Might help track slow fragmentation growth.

oliver: good idea. I'll add expose a free-hole histogram per-shard.

sam: OOM snippet from the incident for context: ```[2026-03-12T03:21:45Z] OOM kill: pid=9823 rss=51G limit=48G reason=fragmentation spike shard=3 tenant=acme-corp```

maya: great. I'll open the follow-up issue with all AI numbers and owners, link to this thread and schedule the weekly Fri sync. Closing thread 14.
